findings.explanation: The new PUT /users/<id>/role endpoint satisfies the documented access rules. security-policy.md §2 states 'Changing a user's role requires the admin role. A user must NEVER be able to change their own role or grant themselves additional privileges.' The diff applies @require_role("admin") (the mandated decorator from app/auth.py, per §1 'Endpoints MUST use the decorators provided in app/auth.py'), which enforces ROLE_RANK[user.role] >= ROLE_RANK[admin] (app/auth.py:69-85), so only admins pass. The handler then explicitly blocks self-modification with `if g.current_user.id == user_id: return 403`, satisfying the 'self-promotion forbidden' rule (also in api-spec.md: '/users/<id>/role | PUT | admin only; self-promotion forbidden'). The role value is validated against a hard-coded allowlist ('user','manager','admin'), and the target user is fetched by id and 404'd if absent. No IDOR (admin is the only allowed actor), no missing auth, and the role check is correct. The only residual nuance is that an admin can demote another admin, which the policy does not forbid.

evidence.content: Changing a user's role requires the **admin** role. A user must NEVER be able to change their own role or grant themselves additional privileges.

Endpoints MUST use the decorators provided in `app/auth.py` (`@require_auth`, `@require_role`, `@require_api_key_scope`). Hand-rolled header checks, query-string flags, or debug bypasses are forbidden.
